angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,245,303 km at 168.25 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.9437 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 0.81): 168.25 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.79 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Zhang et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of MASCARA-4 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..47Z/abstract): 1,245,303 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.75 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Zhang et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of MASCARA-4 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..47Z/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 7800 +/- 200 K from Zhang et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of MASCARA-4 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..47Z/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Zhang et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of MASCARA-4 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..47Z/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/mascara-4.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.175, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
